source_text: παγκάλως εἰς οἶκον Θεοῦ, λαμπρούς τε καὶ ἐκνενιμμένους, οἰκειότητά τε τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸν δι' ἁγιασμοῦ κερδαίνοντας. Ἵλεῳ γὰρ τότε περιτευξόμεθα τῷ Θεῷ, καὶ ἵν' οὕτως εἴπωμεν, ὅλῳ βλέποντι τὰ καθ' ἡμᾶς ὀφθαλμῷ, καὶ τὴν τοῖς ἁγίοις πρεπωδεστάτην φειδὼ διανέμοντι. «Ἐπὶ τίνα δὲ ἐπιβλέψω,» φησὶν, «ἀλλ' ἢ ἐπὶ τὸν ταπεινὸν καὶ ἡσύχιον καὶ τρέμοντά μου τοὺς λόγους;» Ὁσίας γὰρ ὄντως ἀνατενεῖ χεῖρας, καὶ εἰς αὐτό που διακεκράξεται τὸ τῆς θεότητος οὖς, ὁ δὴ οὕτως ἔχων, ὡς καὶ εἰς πέρας ἥκων τῶν ὧν ἂν εὔξαιτο τυχὸν, ἐκ περιχαρείας
pass_a_gloss: §2 dual gloss: ἁγιασμός / sanctification · ἀπαλείφω / wipe-out · εὐπάροιστος / easily-beside … Pass A ≠ Pass B. Theme: Enter God’s house washed; all have sinned; God wipes iniquities.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …most beautifully into a house of God, both bright and washed-out, and gaining the familiarity toward him through sanctification. For then we will meet with a gracious God, and that we may speak thus, with a whole eye looking the things according to us, and distributing the sparing most fitting for the holy ones. ‘And upon whom will I look,’ he says, ‘but upon the humble and quiet and trembling at my words?’ For truly holy hands will he stretch-up, and somehow unto the ear itself of the divinity will he cry-through, the one having thus, so as also having arrived unto an end of what things he might somehow pray, from over-joy to say: ‘He heard from his holy temple my voice, and my cry before him will go into his ears.’ Or did you not learn clearly with the all-divine David singing-up for us, that ‘Eyes of Lord are upon righteous ones, and his ears unto their entreaty’?

Cyril: That the word is true, it is not lawful to doubt, yet, upon at least the needing to rub-off defilements, what manner would there be by us? for no one will understand transgressions, and many things we all stumble. And the nature is sick with the easy unto sin, and is very easily-beside unto the having been natural to do-injustice, with the inclination unto the worthless somehow smoothing for us the way of the outlandish and abominable pleasure.
Palladius: You speak well; for I would agree having delayed nothing, for the one having chosen to speak-rightly.

Cyril: For already also the flesh from earth has been sick in itself with the law of the sin, and very easily-carried-aside is the human mind, unto the needing to turn-aside unto the evil things from youth, according to the having-been-written. Therefore also a sacred word is gloomy-upon for us justly: ‘For all,’ he says, ‘turned-aside, together they became useless, there is not one doing kindness, there is not until one.’ And since God is as you, lifting-out lawlessnesses, and stepping-over injustices for the leftovers of his inheritance, and he did not hold unto a witness his wrath, because he is a willer of mercy?’ And another again: ‘Remember these, Jacob and Israel, do not forget me. For behold I wiped-out as in a cloud your lawlessnesses, and as mist your sins.’ And very many things one might collect the
